question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse scheduling mode in agent-core now, and should early execution be gated on explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata?
rationale: The source-level opportunity is clear, but the change alters core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than fixing a narrow broken contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep the issue open and require an owner design for early scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Wait For Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Block this scheduling change until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract is decided.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Leave current post-stream parallel batching as the supported behavior if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require an owner design for early scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal points to agent-core and AI runtime ownership around the affected scheduling and provider-stream surfaces.
